title: Israel Kills 12 in Lebanon Strikes on Eve of Washington Peace Talks — Third Round of Direct Negotiations Confirmed for May 14–15
detail: Israeli military strikes killed 12 people in Lebanon on May 13, 2026 — the day before the third round of Lebanon–Israel direct talks scheduled in Washington for May 14–15. The strikes represent a grave escalatory event on the eve of the most consequential diplomatic session in decades, placing Lebanon's delegation in a politically untenable position: attend the Washington talks under ongoing Israeli fire, or yield to Hezbollah's demand to abandon the direct format. Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem had publicly called on the Lebanese government to withdraw from the direct talks on May 12, characterizing the Washington format as a 'concession to the enemy' and insisting on indirect negotiations through intermediaries. The May 14–15 Washington session — the third round of direct Lebanon–Israel diplomacy — will be facilitated by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The Israeli delegation is led by Ron Dermer; Lebanon's delegation by Simon Karam. The agenda covers: security arrangements along the Blue Line, Israeli military withdrawal under UNSC Resolution 1701, Hezbollah's armed presence south of the Litani River, detainee releases, displaced civilians, reconstruction funding, and a proposed ceasefire extension (the current framework expires around May 17). Lebanon's PM Nawaf Salam and President Joseph Aoun invested significant political capital in the Washington format as the only viable path to full Israeli withdrawal and post-war reconstruction. The US State Department confirmed the meeting via a formal spokesperson release. The fundamental gaps remain: Israel conditions full withdrawal on Hezbollah disarmament; Lebanon insists on unconditional Israeli withdrawal first.

title: Zelensky Publicly Accepts Direct Peace Talks With Putin in Istanbul — Kremlin Has Not Confirmed Putin's Attendance
detail: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky publicly accepted Russia's signal of readiness for direct talks on May 13, 2026, confirming his willingness to meet President Vladimir Putin in Istanbul, Turkey. The diplomatic opening follows Putin's signals around May 10 that the war was 'heading toward an end' and Russia's expressed openness to direct talks in Istanbul or another neutral venue. Zelensky indicated readiness for a meeting around May 15. However, as of May 13, the Kremlin had not confirmed Putin's personal attendance — leaving any diplomatic breakthrough conditional on Russian follow-through. If confirmed, a Zelensky–Putin direct meeting would be the first since March 2022 — the last in-person Ukraine–Russia leader talks since Russia's full-scale invasion began. Turkey and President Erdogan — who have maintained dialogue with both Moscow and Kyiv throughout the war — are the proposed hosts, and Turkey has confirmed its readiness to facilitate. The Istanbul venue carries historical resonance: March–April 2022 Istanbul negotiations between Ukrainian and Russian delegations came close to a draft agreement before collapsing. The diplomatic opening comes just two days after the US-brokered 72-hour ceasefire expired on May 11–12 with Russia immediately resuming large-scale drone attacks (200+ Shahed drones and cruise missiles at Ukrainian cities). The EU separately discussed direct EU–Russia dialogue during a foreign ministers meeting on May 11. The only concrete outcome of the May 9–11 ceasefire — a 1,000-per-side prisoner of war exchange — continues to proceed and represents the framework's only tangible deliverable. Core gaps remain unbridged: Russia demands recognition of all four annexed oblasts (Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson); Ukraine refuses territorial concessions without NATO-equivalent security guarantees.

title: Iran Parliament Threatens Weapons-Grade 90% Uranium Enrichment if Attacked Again — US–Iran MOU Deadlocked With No New Round Scheduled
detail: As US–Iran MOU negotiations remained completely deadlocked through May 13, 2026, senior Iranian lawmakers escalated nuclear deterrence rhetoric. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and MP Ebrahim Rezaei publicly warned that Iran would enrich uranium to 90% — weapons-grade — if Iran was attacked again, according to reporting by Euronews and Al-Arabiya on May 12–13. Iran currently holds approximately 400–460 kg of uranium enriched to 60%, a stockpile that US and Israeli officials assess could be upgraded to weapons-grade within one to two weeks using existing centrifuge infrastructure. The 90% enrichment threat represents a significant escalation in domestic political pressure on Iran's negotiating position: if the legislature is publicly committing to a nuclear breakout response to any attack, the space for a compromise MOU framework narrows severely. The state of negotiations as of May 13: Trump declared the ceasefire 'on massive life support' on May 12; the US Treasury and State Departments imposed new targeted sanctions on Iranian nuclear research entities and China–Iran ballistic missile supply chains; Iran's 14-point MOU counterproposal (submitted May 10 via Pakistan back-channel) was rejected by Trump as 'totally unacceptable'; and CNN confirmed a 'clash of perceptions' — Iran demands comprehensive sanctions relief, security guarantees, and enrichment rights as preconditions; the US insists on a narrow ceasefire-first MOU deferring all comprehensive issues to a 30-day negotiating window. No new round of talks is scheduled. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed for the third consecutive month, with approximately 750 commercial vessels trapped and US gas prices at their highest level since July 2022 ($4.48/gal). Trump is traveling to China during this period, creating a possible indirect diplomatic back-channel through Beijing.
